prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Create ONE high-fidelity complete screen for HEAV3NS-CODE, a native macOS workspace for the LUMI coding agent. This is a product journey concept, not a website. Flat straight-on screenshot, entire app window fills a 1600x1000 landscape 16:10 image. No perspective, desktop wallpaper, presentation frame, annotations, labels outside the app, or collage.
Shared visual language: a carefully crafted native macOS shell with IDE density and navigation learned from VS Code and Xcode. Neutral graphite window and sidebar (#20242b), deeper code canvas (#171b21), subtly lighter title bar (#282d35), off-white readable text (#edf1f6), secondary text (#b3becd), and restrained blue (#3985f5) for selection and primary actions. Thin separators, natural 6–10px native control corners, SF-style system text and SF Mono-style code. Precise alignment and readable 14–16px body type at this image size. Do not make a generic web dashboard, large marketing headline, bento layout, neon/glass design, or chunky card collage. macOS traffic lights at top left. Product name exact: HEAV3NS-CODE (digit 3). Project name exact: LUMI-NEW.
Every screen uses the same restrained typography, palette, window chrome, and recognizable controls. Short copy is rendered verbatim. These are illustrative prototype states; do not invent factual metrics, prices, model versions, customer claims, account data, or shipped functionality. No invented company logos. Use plain product typography when no logo is provided.
For sign-in states: the app offers Sign in with ChatGPT and hands off to the system browser. Do not paint an in-app password, email, or API-key form or a counterfeit OpenAI login page. Sign-in and AI plan permission are distinct. Show plan-enabled state only in the explicitly described authorized example.
For workspace states: inspection remains read-only and says so. File tabs and syntax tint are visual navigation proposals. No stage, commit, apply, deploy, automatic file deletion, debugger, terminal, or extension-store controls. Show files as a directory hierarchy and classes as an Outline inside the active file, never disguise classes as disk folders.

SCREEN 11: Inspect the changes
Completed task and change inspection in the SAME IDE shell. Workspace shell: 48px native title bar with traffic lights, small project switcher "LUMI-NEW", central command field "Search files and symbols", right "Connected" and a Stop control. A narrow 76px navigation rail on the far left contains consistent outline icons WITH visible small labels: "Explorer", "Search", "Changes", "Sessions"; bottom "Projects" and "Account". Explorer is selected unless this scene says otherwise. Next a 280px Explorer pane. Center about 810px is the read-only file canvas. Right about 420px is the LUMI conversation pane. Bottom thin status bar reads "main" at left and "Swift · UTF-8 · Read only" at right. No duplicate navigation icons. A project tree with restrained indent guides and folder chevrons shows "LUMI-NEW", "native", "Sources", "Heav3nsCode", then Swift files "App.swift", "WorkspaceWindow.swift", "NavigationSidebar.swift", "RuntimeClient.swift", "ApprovalReview.swift". Beneath the expanded Sources branch are "Tests" and "Package.swift"; at root "src", "docs", "README.md". Use understated orange Swift file icons, blue folders, and clear selected-row fill; filenames never collide with icons or truncate unnecessarily. An "OUTLINE" section belongs below the file tree, with small type glyphs for class, property, and method. The right LUMI pane always has a visible composer at its bottom, Send or Queue, plus "Using ChatGPT plan" and "Manage usage" as small account affordances. Use standard toolbar, disclosure and source-list affordances, rather than blocks of decorative cards. Navigation rail Changes selected, Explorer rail inactive. Replace only the Explorer pane contents with heading "Changes", segment "Working Tree" selected / "Staged", section "MODIFIED · 2", file rows "WorkspaceWindow.swift" selected with small M indicator, "NavigationSidebar.swift" M. Below subtle text "Includes pre-existing and external edits". Central active tab "WorkspaceWindow.swift — Changes"; breadcrumb shows native › Sources › Heav3nsCode. Header "Working tree vs HEAD" plus read-only label. Central unified diff is readable, restrained red deletion and green addition lines, gutter plus/minus signs and line numbers. Sample content "@@ Workspace layout @@", "- stack.spacing = 6", "+ stack.spacing = 10", "  stack.alignment = .leading", then second small hunk "@@ Sidebar rows @@", "- table.rowHeight = 42", "+ table.rowHeight = 36". Keep remainder quiet without fabricating huge code. Right LUMI pane shows "Task finished", concise response "The sidebar spacing is clearer. Inspect both files before continuing.", two understated disclosure rows "Updated workspace spacing", "Prepared change summary", and evidence note "Checks not run · Not reviewed". No checkmark claiming all tests passed. Footer in LUMI shows composer "Explain the changes." and Send. Using ChatGPT plan and Manage usage remain visible. No large metrics, fake approvals, stage/commit/apply/undo buttons, terminal, or review claim.

Input image roles: preserve the supplied HEAV3NS-CODE reference's native identity, shared dark material and typography. Where a prior screen is supplied, preserve the app's design system while replacing only the screen content with this scene. Any VS Code image is a navigation reference, never content, branding or annotations to copy.
